translation:
So that's what we went with. I decided to take
Nagato with me to the computer society…
Hey, Nagato. Can I ask you something?
What?

You know how we just entered class 1-10 a
moment ago?

Did you see what happened before that? A
silhouette was floating outside the window…

Well, I know what I'm saying is strange. At any
rate, it was on the second floor.

Maybe I'm just seeing things. I dismissed it at
first, but there was also that classroom.

If Haruhi said, "I wish for that!” even a
ghost parade could manifest into reality.
Was that also Haruhi's doing?
Are you listening, Nagato?
I'm listening.

If that's the case, why don't you give me a
reply or two?

At this rate, whether we can get anything
out of those guys gives me endless anxiety.

If you're wondering if Nagato is well suited to
witness investigation, the answer is NO.

…I'll just end up suffering, after all. That's
what always happens…

Since I joined the Haruhi faction, I feel as
though I've grown mentally.
Although I'm not entirely happy about that…

Which reminds me, Nagato, have you been
getting value out of that PC in the clubroom?
Nagato silently gave a slight tilt of the head.

I just felt like the so-called "personal
computer” would be a good fit for Nagato.

You see, there's lots of things it can be used
for.

For example, you can search through the
library's collection of books or something.
No need.
I know of all of the books in the library.

…Then, if I were to ask you if they had a
specific book, could you answer?
Possibly.

In that case, it's pointless to look it up on a
PC, huh…

Don't tell me this person has already read
through the library's entire catalog…?
No, it's nothing, forget about it.
I see.

Come to think of it, Nagato might have
something even more impressive than a PC.

But if that's the case, then our PC is nothing
more than a waste of space, isn't it?

It probably goes without saying, but the room
was riddled with computers.

The thought arises every time I come here,
but this place reeks of brand-new electronics.

It gave off a similar impression to the
electronics section at a mass retailer.
Then, the computer society members…

…were directly facing their monitors and fully
absorbed in striking their keyboards.

It seems like they're in the middle of something
important, so I'll wait a bit.

How are they able to gather so many people
during summer vacation?

But then again, I'm in no position to comment
on other people's business.

Much to my dismay, the SOS Brigade is also
wrapped up in its infamous club activities.

I'm guessing that Nagato's silence isn't
because she's calculating the right timing.

Looks like I'll have to make the first move
after all.

Huh? You guys are back again? What the hell
is it this time?!

Thankfully, the other party called out to me
first.

As you can see, we're busy! If you've come to
disturb us, get out!

I didn't expect a warm welcome, but I didn't
anticipate such a cold-hearted one either.

We're not here to disturb you. We wanted to
hear the story from before in more detail…

Story from before? Ahh… that ghost story,
huh?
…We already told your club president, right?

If you mean Haruhi, she's off doing something
on her own.

I'd like to add that he can relax, but that
would be awkward. I'll just keep that to myself.
I see… Then I guess it's fine.

Actually,
no, it's not fine. I really am busy right now.
It only needs to take a second.

You could just say it was a mere misjudgment,
or misunderstanding, or something.

I just want to go over the eyewitness
testimonies again.

Wow… You guys sure have it rough, having to
work under her. Sounds troublesome.
Of all things, he started sympathizing with me.

Though at times I've certainly wished that
there was someone who understood.

And yet, now that it's actually happened, why
does it feel so uncomfortable?

And you there… You were in the literary club,
weren't you? Poor thing.

Come to think of it, Nagato was in the literary
club, and our clubroom was theirs.

To be honest, it should've stayed that way…
Probably.

Nagato, you're still technically in the literary
club, aren't you?
I am.

Even now, the clubroom is also more or less
under the literary club's ownership.
Yes.

In other words, you've completely rented out
the room, Haruhi.

Actually, it benefits no one to call it
"renting.”

"Give an inch, and they'll take a mile” is a
more appropriate term for this situation.

Haruhi has the nerve to just take the whole
mile from the very start.

Right now, Nagato is a member of the SOS
Brigade, and that's good enough for me.

Though, the literary club, huh… if I'm not
mistaken, Nagato was the only member.

I haven't seen anything in the clubroom that
suggests they assigned any club activities.

I'm surprised the club hasn't been shut down.
It's still going, even in such a state.

I sympathize with your situation, but how
many times do I have to tell you that we're—
B-big trouble! Presideeent!
The server is… Our data storage is…!
Wh-what is it?! What's going on?

We've got big trouble! It won't boot up
anymore! It's not responding!
What the hell…?! Reboot it again!

No matter how many times I try, it doesn't
seem to work… It might be the hardware…

What about the backups?! All the data was
copied, as it should've been, right?!

That's… Not yet… I was just about to, but it
completely stopped working…

That sure was noisy. Seems like a pretty
dreadful situation is transpiring.

Unbelievable… To think you were just about
to…

The president had an expression of despair
resembling Munch's masterpiece, "The Scream.”

Looks like there's something wrong with your
computer…

All our hard work… Our entire summer of toil is
completely wasted…
Ohh, even though we made this much…

President, everyone… I'm sorry. If only I had
backed it up sooner…

The air is heavy like a funeral wake. It might
be too late to hear the story now.
Wait, hold on…?

Maybe I can use this situation to get them to
lower their guard a little.
Nagato, can't you do something about this?
Do what?

It seems like these guys have a problem.
What's happening here? Can you fix it?

Nagato stared blankly at the broken
computer before eventually…
It is possible.

Could I ask you to help? I don't particularly
have a reason to do them any favors, but…
It might put them in a bit of a better mood.
Understood.

Ah… Mr. President. The truth is, Nagato here
is very knowledgeable about computers.
She might be able to fix it.

You really mean it?! You can actually do
that?!
Nagato, please fix it.
Commencing repairs.

Nagato stood in front of the broken PC… And
suddenly plugged it into the wall outlet.
Wha…?!
Finished.
Wha?! P-p-p-president!

What is it this time…? What else could possibly
have gone wrong…?

I-it booted up! The server suddenly
restarted…!
R-really?! How's the data?!
Give me a second… It's okay, it's all still there!

It is recommended to make a backup
immediately.

Make a backup right away! And then, run a
virus scan too!

Ahh, thank goodness… For a moment there I
didn't know what was going to happen…

The president was trembling with emotion as if
to say, "Thank you, God!”

It seems your machine troubles blew over
without a hitch. Very good, very good.

Ahh… You two just witnessed something
outrageous. I'm sure it was surprising.

My heart nearly stopped… Anyways, I'm
relieved. Good grief.
But how exactly were you able to fix it?
It seemed like you repaired it in no time.

I don't honestly need to inform him that it was
just unplugged from the outlet, do I?

I'll do what I can here to preserve his sense
of gratitude.

Well, it seems like that was very important
data.
Are you making a program or something?
…So, I asked something unrelated.
Oh? Are you interested?

It's just as you say! We're working on some-
thing that will make computer society history.

Well you see, we're making what you would
refer to as a "game program.”

Well, it's really just extremely back-breaking
work. It's an immense task.

What happened to their wariness towards us?
The president seems to be in a good mood.

We even had quite an argument over choosing
a programming language.

Though, I'm glad we decided to go
object-oriented, because of those specs.

See, there's only so much you're able to do
with a standard library, right?

On top of that, the GUI was a huge issue, and
the screen design problem too…

Jargon started flying out all over the place. I
don't understand any of this at all.

But unlike me, Nagato was listening quietly. I
wonder if she understands it?

In addition, we've finished writing most of the
source code.

My, how fascinating. As one would expect of
the experts at the computer society.

Y-you think so? I wouldn't take it that far.
Ahahaha…
On the dawn of it's completion, you guys'—
…Ah, that's right.

Suddenly, the president covered his mouth.
What is it, all of a sudden?

…Weren't you two also members of that SOS
group, now that I think about it?
Unfortunately, I cant deny that.
Never mind, please forget about it.

From the beginning, this was a topic that I
couldn't follow, so I won't pursue it any further.
…Information gathering.

That's right, we want to hear the story
concerning the classroom from before.

Ah, class 1-10 ghost stories and the like. I
think we already said everything last time.

Is there anything you forgot to mention?
Even if just a minor detail…?

Hey, is there anything you forgot to bring up
about the class 1-10 thing?

The president called out to Club Member A who
was working in front of the server.
Umm…

Forgive me, but I can't seem to remember. I do
feel like there was something though.
But, is it really that important?

A global crisis is taking place! Or at least
that's what I'd like to say…
The backup and virus scan are complete~
Alright, we're back in business.
You guys… I'm sorry but, if you don't mind…

It doesn't seem like I'll be able to get anything
more out of them. Are we out of time…?
Sorry for bothering you at such a busy time.
Nagato, let's pull out now.

I might have been imagining it, but for just a
moment, Nagato's face seemed disappointed.

Nagato… Did she want to stay here a bit
longer and keep listening? Well, I never.

Nagato, do you want to stay and talk a bit
more?
Why?
Well… I can't really justify why, but…

I thought you might be interested in listening
to the president more, or in the club equipment.
Just a little.
However, it is fine.
Really…? Alright then, if you say so.

I wonder how the computer society's
equipment and program look in Nagato's eyes.

Either way, I didn't expect that listening to
them talk would end up becoming such a clamor.

This summer camp just started, so I'm worried
about what the future holds…

In the end, it seems I couldn't get any new
info at all. Good grief…
Well then, I'm not sure what to do from here.
Talk to her some more
Don't talk to her any more
Get confirmation from Nagato
Don't ask for details
Do you want to stay a bit longer?
It's probably just my imagination.
